organization.name: The Chartered Duel Corps
organization.entry:
The Chartered Duel Corps is Fogport’s official organization of licensed professional duelists. They are hired by wealthy citizens, noble houses, merchants, industrialists, foreign envoys, and important officials who have been challenged to a duel but do not wish to risk their own lives.

In Fogport, a duel may settle an insult, debt, business dispute, political accusation, romantic grievance, or matter of honor. The wealthy have therefore purchased the right to outsource courage.

The Charter

The Corps exists because the Civic Order decided that private violence was too important to leave unregulated. The official reasoning was: “A regulated duel is preferable to an unregulated feud.” The less official reasoning is that every legally recognized killing generates a fee.

The Masks

Every member wears a nearly identical standardized pale mask. The masks conceal identity, prevent family grudges from following a duelist home, and make the wearer appear to be an instrument of the Charter rather than a private person.

A Chartered Duelist does not fight as a particular family, gender, species, profession, or citizen. They fight as the representative of a legally recognized claim. The mask is officially a Civic Anonymity Faceplate. Everyone else calls it a Charter Mask, or simply a Mask.

Uniform

The Corps wears a practical, unisex uniform of dark charcoal and blue-black cloth: high-collared split-tail coat, waistcoat or armored vest, matching trousers, high boots, gloves, leather belt, reinforced bracers, dull brass shoulder guards, pale piping, numbered badge plates, and a short ceremonial mantle.

The uniform is designed to look equally authoritative on men, women, Lumenati, pigmen, Thrallo, and any other citizen legally permitted to serve. The state wants the Corps to appear disciplined, anonymous, and interchangeable.

Lumenati Duelists

A small number of Lumenati hold Chartered Duelist licenses. Their spell-reel backpacks are modified to comply with Corps regulations. They may use defensive wards, illumination, sound suppression, controlled force, fog manipulation, medical reels, and carefully restricted offensive magic.

The Duel Process

A legal duel involves an astonishing amount of paperwork. The challenger must submit the names of both parties, the grievance, weapons, location, time, witnesses, expected audience, likely amount of blood, corpse ownership, street-cleaning responsibility, and possible municipal damage.

The Bureau of Public Challenge classifies the duel as personal, commercial, aristocratic, diplomatic, romantic, political, theatrical, religious, industrial, or too embarrassing to classify.

Once approved, the state assigns a venue, Civic Duel Referee, medical examiner, recorder, corpse clerk, street-clearance crew, and Civic Vigilance representative. The referee’s first duty is to ensure that the duel remains taxable.

Duelist Contracts

Contracts may require fighting until first blood, surrender, incapacity, death, protection for one encounter or an entire day, preventing a challenger from reaching a client, defeating a named opponent, protecting a client’s reputation, or making a death appear honorable.

Specialists include sword duelists, pistol duelists, long-range marksmen, Lumen magic duelists, nonhuman-opponent specialists, tram fighters, close-quarters fighters, and experts at protecting clients while fighting.

Fees

Clients pay for skill, preparation, silence, wardrobe, travel, witnesses, medical care, legal protection, and consequence management. Additional charges apply for fog, rain, fire, crowds, rooftops, moving trams, unstable bridges, monster interference, magical complications, foreign weapons, public embarrassment, inconvenient corpses, and surviving witnesses.

Reputation

The Corps is admired by the wealthy, resented by ordinary citizens, and hated by people who believe honor should require personal risk. Among the upper classes, hiring a Chartered Duelist is tasteful. Among the poor, it proves that the rich have found a way to make even bravery hereditary.

Civic Duel Referees

The Corps does not control its own duels. Every official duel is overseen by a referee from the Bureau of Public Challenge, assisted by a clerk from the Bureau of Civic Measurement. They determine when the duel begins, what counts as a legal strike, whether magic has exceeded its limits, whether surrender is sincere, and whether the duel has generated enough public interest to justify a second round.

Secrets and Scandals

Some duelists accept secret contracts. Some wealthy clients manufacture insults to arrange legal assassinations. Some referees alter terms after being paid by both sides. Some masks have been recovered from dead duelists whose bodies were never found.

The most serious accusation is that the Civic Vigilance maintains a private roster of duelists for political killings. Officially, the Corps fights only for clients. Unofficially, certain Masks fight for the Civic Order itself.

Player Character Hooks

  • A wealthy client hires the characters to escort a Chartered Duelist through the Shambles.
  • A duel is approved against an opponent who died three days earlier.
  • A Mask asks the characters to investigate an altered contract.
  • A duel on a tram reveals that the tram carries something more dangerous than passengers.
  • A Lumenati Duelist’s reel pack contains an unlisted spell.
  • A masked duelist is found dead, but the mask is still warm.
  • A citizen hires the Corps to defend them from an accusation that is actually true.
  • The Civic Vigilance orders the characters to find a former duelist who knows who controls the Corps.
  • A duel in the former Royal Opera Theater is interrupted when one empty senate seat begins applauding.
  • Byl is challenged by someone who hired the most expensive Mask in Fogport.

post.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Chartered Duel Corps
post.entry:
PRIVATE / GM-RESTRICTED

The Chartered Duel Corps exists to make violence look civilized. It transforms personal hatred into paperwork, murder into service, and cowardice into a respectable professional expense.

The Civic Order tells the city that the Corps protects honor.

The wealthy know better.

The Corps protects the wealthy from having to risk their own skins.
